title: Ratatouille
subtitle: Provençal slow-cooked vegetable stew
excerpt: Aubergine, courgette, red pepper, and tomato slow-cooked in olive oil with garlic and herbs until they collapse into a silky, deeply flavoured Provençal stew.

recipe.sourceNotes: Ratatouille is the great summer vegetable dish of Provence, taking its name from the Provençal 'ratatolha'. The dish was originally a peasant recipe using the surplus vegetables of the summer garden. The key vegetables are aubergine, courgette, tomato, red pepper, and onion, all cooked in abundant olive oil with garlic, thyme, and bay. The debate about the correct method of preparing ratatouille is longstanding: the traditional method cooks all the vegetables together in one pan; a more refined method (associated with Joël Robuchon and popularised by the Pixar film of the same name) fries each vegetable separately to preserve its individual character before combining them. The single-pan method is given here. Ratatouille is excellent hot or cold, and improves considerably on the second day as the flavours meld.

recipeTools.notes: A large, wide, deep saucepan or casserole dish with a lid.

content.text: Salt the aubergine cubes in a colander for 20 minutes. This draws out moisture and stops the aubergine soaking up too much oil. Add the vegetables in stages, not all at once: the onion and pepper go in first, then the aubergine, then the courgette, then the tomato. Each takes a different amount of time. Add very little liquid: the vegetables release plenty of their own moisture as they cook.

items.preparation: cut into 2 cm cubes; salted and drained
deseeded and cut into 2 cm pieces
ripe; roughly chopped, or 1 x 400 g tin

content.text: Pat the salted aubergine dry. Heat 3 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large, wide pan over medium-high heat. Fry the aubergine in batches until golden, about 5 minutes per batch. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the pan. Fry the onion and pepper over medium heat for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, thyme, and bay. Cook for 1 minute. Add the courgette and cook for 5 minutes.

Return the aubergine to the pan. Add the tomatoes and season with salt and pepper. Stir, reduce the heat to low, and cover. Cook for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until all the vegetables are very tender and the sauce has thickened. Remove the thyme and bay. Tear in the basil and serve warm or at room temperature.
